Header: Xanthomonas campestris pv campestris Kuola kwa kabichi

Prevention: Use certified seed and seedlings free from disease as this disease can be seed- borne.
Correct plant spacing: 50 cm between plants and 60 cm between rows.
Do not plant crucifers in areas that have a history of the disease.
Rotate crucifers 3-4 years with crops that are not susceptible, such as maize, legumes and tomato.
Avoid flood/furrow irrigation because it will carry the disease from infected to uninfected areas.
Avoid moving through fields when the plants are wet to prevent disease spread.
Destroy alternative host weeds in the crucifer family e.g. birdsrape mustard, Indian mustard and black mustard.
Monitoring: Additional relevant crops: cauliflower, chinese cabbage, brussel sprouts, turnip, mustard, broccoli, rape and radish.
Monitor plants weekly for symptoms from planting.
V-shaped lesions with the open part of 'V' along the edge of the leaf.
The diseased leaf area becomes brown and brittle.
Affected leaf veins turn dark brown to black.
V-shaped lesions enlarge and the entire leaf eventually turns yellow or wilts and falls from the plant.
Infected seedlings remain stunted and become unproductive.
There is a ring of black discoloured tissue within the stem when cut.
If 6-8 plants/ha show symptoms, take action.
Direct Control: Destroy crop residue by drying and burning.
Seeds of cabbage, broccoli and brussel sprouts should be hot water treated at 122°F (50°C) for 25 minutes.
Seeds of cauliflower, kale and turnip should be hot water treated at 122°F (50°C) for 15 minutes.
Restrictions: Use personal protective equipment when handling and applying pesticides, follow the label recommendations.
Do not eat, drink or smoke when mixing or applying pesticides.
Copper-based pesticides can be used to reduce the spread of the disease:
Apply copper hydroxide (500 g/kg) (Funguran-OH WP, Cungfu 583
SC) at a rate of 150 ml/100
Apply at sight of disease and every 7-14 days.
Ensure full coverage of the plant.

Apply at sight of disease and every 7-14 days.
